changes.before:
(
BUILD ONLY · NOT APPLICATION UI
Peer-set ownership
A research cohort is explicit and versioned: selected issuer + peer identities + reason each is included. Do not turn the analyst cohort into a universal “peer score” or company rank. Reuse Data OS issuer/security/listing identities.
Clock + period law
Bind one knowledge cutoff and each issuer publication timestamp, fiscal-period start/end and source revision. Default to latest-known-by-cutoff, not a guessed same-calendar quarter. A later peer result creates a new state, never a silent rewrite.
Metric comparability
Every row carries metric definition, GAAP/non-GAAP basis, currency/unit, business taxonomy and comparability status. “Not comparable” keeps the facts visible but withholds a normalized delta. Missing data is unavailable—not zero or peer median.
Normalization is a method
Any adjustment must name the company, input source, transformation and reason. Keep raw reported values accessible beside the normalized view. Never infer segment remapping, interpolate missing periods or normalize from narrative alone.
Interaction + evidence
Changing cutoff, cohort or normalization invalidates selected comparison rows and local AI context until new inputs are bound. Source actions open the exact issuer document/period and return to the selected company/metric/focus/scroll.
Responsive behavior
At 390/320px use stacked company cards + metric-by-metric comparability sheets. Do not compress three desktop columns or hide fiscal dates. 44px actions, full labels and explicit basis remain.
Acceptance
Test mismatched fiscal calendars, later publication after cutoff, source correction, currency/unit/basis mismatch, missing peer result, one-time adjustment, rights denial, cohort change, keyboard order and return restoration. No ranking/signal/trade semantic may emerge from display order.
)
